main_body: Whole Japanese-style building seen straight on: a blue-grey tile roof with a ridge cap and corner finials, a cream plaster band with slit windows, a lower eave roof, then a dark wood lattice wall with a central doorway and straw/hay piles at the base.
top_band: Rows 1-5 form a blue-grey ridge band (L 158/130/83/130/83) with an outline above it. Rows 7-28 are the roof tile face (L 130 to 104), which stays in the same family as the roof body and has no distinct front-edge step. No separate horizontal surface sits above a front face.
evidence: The roof is a vertical-striped tile face drawn flat, with only a thin ridge cap above it. The plaster band, lower eave and lattice wall are stacked flat bands viewed face-on. The lower roof strip (rows 41-47) is also a flat band with no visible slope. The wooden lattice and door are painted flat, not inset. The scan shows no top surface separated by a step or edge line, so the whole drawing reads as an architectural front elevation. The references show lit roof slopes that clearly sit above the walls.

style.evidence: The candidate has 7 colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references, and 33 distinct colours against 185 and 66. Its dark edge pixels are 72% neutral, against 7-9% for the references, which gives the near-black sticker look. The roof has a few tile-stripe steps, but they are regular and mechanical, with no per-tile scallops or highlights. The plaster and lattice are simple repeated patterns. Flat-fill coverage is low at 3%, but overall it is thinner and flatter than the references.
